claude_code.how: For CLI-based agent access, configure/import the selected MCP server, inspect its relevant tools, then use a small per-server or per-workflow skill that invokes mcporter call; upstream discourages one generic skill teaching every server. A dedicated generated CLI is another option for repeated workflows. If pooled native MCP access is actually wanted, upstream separately supports mcporter serve --servers <selected> --stdio; that optional bridge is documented at https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/docs/cli-reference.md .

codex.how: The same focused CLI/skill pattern works from Codex shell commands and scripts. Codex can also register the optional mcporter serve --stdio bridge for selected keep-alive servers, but native mcp_servers registrations can connect directly to each upstream server and do not inherently traverse mcporter. The bridge publishes server__tool names; importing Codex config into mcporter is not the reverse operation of routing Codex through it.

official_baseline_claims.claim: Upstream defines mcporter as a TypeScript runtime and CLI for discovering and invoking MCP servers from terminals, scripts, agents and generated CLIs; it supports ad-hoc URL/stdio targets and imports several native clients' server configurations. These are transport and workflow capabilities, not a published token-compression percentage.

Upstream's agent-skill guidance recommends small per-server skills so agents do not load irrelevant server schemas; it presents prompt-size economy as a workflow design benefit without a quantitative savings guarantee for this host.

limitations.text: npm installs require Node 24 or newer. The package's CLI/runtime and optional native standalone distributions are distinct installation choices.

File-backed string arguments are supported as key=@path or --key @path; @@ escapes a literal leading @. --args/--params accept a JSON object, and source also supports --args - for JSON read from stdin (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/src/cli/call-arguments.ts#L317). This is a named UTF-8 string facility, not arbitrary binary attachment transport.

In v0.14.1, resolveSelectorAndTool at src/cli/call-arguments.ts:170-171 consumes the first positional token when no --server or expression-provided server is present, even if --tool was supplied; trailing named arguments are parsed afterward. A call must select the target unambiguously before relying on content=@file to reach a required content property. The same source handles --args - at :317-322 and reads @path at :362-386.
The optional mcporter serve MCP bridge exposes only configured keep-alive servers; it is not an automatic interception layer for every MCP connection made by Claude or Codex.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The shared failed headroom compression record is an invocation-shape defect in the fixture, not lack of mcporter file-argument support.
deviations_from_upstream.why: The first command had --name headroom --tool headroom_compress content=@file but no --server; the parser consumes the content token as selector at src/cli/call-arguments.ts:170-171 (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/src/cli/call-arguments.ts#L164), leaving Headroom's required content argument absent. The CLI reference expressly supports key=@path (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/docs/cli-reference.md#mcporter-call-servertool). The corrected headroom card command adds --server headroom and succeeds; the same failed record is intentionally attributed to transport and target under the card's multi-tool counting method.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Use --server headroom --tool headroom_compress content=@file, a complete server.tool selector, or an explicitly serialized JSON payload with an unambiguous target. Preserve the original failure and its corrected result; do not change either assembled card's attribution or numbers.

final_verdict.summary: For its selected Linux CLI-bridge role, installed MCPorter 0.14.1 matches latest stable and the supported upstream architecture; the retained qualification reports 37/37 checks on both candidate and baseline (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/releases/tag/v0.14.1; evidence/receipts/mcporter-0141-qualification-20260925.json). There is no eligible standalone token-reduction comparison or native savings counter: returned-results demonstrate transport and exact cross-process recovery, while attributable token savings remain unverified (cards/mcporter.json#adapted_performance; ../rr/returned-results.json#components/mcporter). The failed shared Headroom call omitted --server, and its corrected invocation succeeds with file-backed content, matching upstream selector parsing and key=@path support (../rr/returned-results.json#headroom-e2e-06-compress-attempt1-failed; #headroom-e2e-06-compress; https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/docs/cli-reference.md). The scan labels 111/1010 Ultracode workflow children (10.99%, 1111 CLI matches), 2/301 eligible Codex workers (0.66%, 2 CLI matches), and 0/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block as users; zero MCP calls is consistent with the selected CLI bridge and direct native server registrations (invoke_by_tool.json; docs/token-session-handbook.md:142). Next, standardize complete selectors for recurring workflows, preserve Node/ps and daemon-version checks, and measure successful useful calls without assigning downstream compression savings to the bridge.
